*1.findings_raw: TPMT*1 is assigned normal function based on definitive evidence. TPMT*1 corresponds to the reference sequence, NG_008807.2, containing no SNVs. As such, TPMT.1 activity is used as the reference for in vitro studies using yeast and mammalian cell expression systems (8561894, 9177237, 13679074, 16220112, 18708949). Erythrocytes from individuals genotyped TPMT*1/*1 exhibited normal to high enzymatic activity (9246020, 15226673, 23252716, 31005613). Lastly, TPMT*1/*1 patients have been shown to tolerate standard thiopurine dosing (23585236, 29387964, 33928426, 27564568, 11304783, 10580024, 19057372).

*10.findings_raw: TPMT*10 is assigned no function based on limited evidence. An individual genotyped TPMT*1/*10 was prescribed 50 mg/day 6-MP and experienced cytopenia after 3 months of treatment (10833476). In vitro studies found TPMT.10 protein expression is comparable to TPMT.1 in mammalian cells (16220112, 18708949) and yeast cells (13679074). TPMT.10 enzymatic activity is decreased by 30-70% in vitro relative to TPMT.1 (13679074, 16220112, 18708949) and TPMT.10 exhibited decreased affinity for 6-TG (18708949). Six out of ten variant effect predictors tested by CPIC staff predict that the TPMT*10-defining SNV, c.430G>C (p.G144R), impairs protein function.

*11.findings_raw: TPMT*11 is assigned no function based on limited evidence. Erythrocytes from a patient genotyped TPMT*3A/*11 exhibited very low enzymatic activity and 6-MMP was undetectable in the patient's plasma and their 6-MP dose was reduced to 15% of the standard dosage (12835738). In vitro studies using mammalian cell expression systems found TPMT.11 protein expression is decreased (16220112). TPMT.11 enzymatic activity is decreased up to 97% in vitro and TPMT.11 exhibied decreased affinity for 6-MP, 6-TG, and SAM relative to TPMT.1 (16220112, 18708949). Seven out of ten variant effect predictors tested by CPIC staff predict that the TPMT*11-defining SNV, c.395G>A (p.C132Y), impairs protein function.

*12.findings_raw: TPMT*12 is assigned uncertain function based on inadequate evidence. Patients genotyped TPMT*1/*12 exhibited TPMT enzymatic activity that is comparable to TPMT*1/*1 patients and there was no difference in 6-MP dose intensity between TPMT*1/*12 and TPMT*1/*1 patients (27564568). In vitro studies using mammalian cell expression systems found that TPMT.12 protein expression is decreased, enzymatic activity is decreased >50%, and TPMT.12 exhibited decreased affinity for 6-TG and SAM compared to TPMT.1 (16220112, 18708949). TPMT.12 also exhibited an increased rate of protein degradation compared to TPMT.1 (16220112). TPMT.12 enzymatic activity is decreased by 75% compared to TPMT.1 in yeast cells (13679074). An additional in vitro study found that TPMT.12 protein abundance in mammalian cells was comparable to TPMT.1 (29785012). Four out of ten variant effect predictors tested by CPIC staff predict that the TPMT*12-defining SNV, c.374C>T (p.S125L), impairs protein function.

*14.findings_raw: TPMT*14 is assigned no function based on moderate evidence. Four out of eight variant effect predictors tested by CPIC staff predict that the TPMT*14-defining SNV, c.1A>G (p.M1V), impairs protein function. c.1A>G (p.M1V) is predicted to disrupt protein translation due to the loss of the canonical start codon, and there is no alternative start codon available

*15.findings_raw: TPMT*15 is assigned no function based on limited evidence. Erythrocytes from a patient genotyped TPMT*3A/*15 exhibited very low enzymatic activity (15083071, 31005613). *16.findings_raw: TPMT*16 is assigned no function based on moderate evidence. An in silico prediction model of TPMT variant functionality can predict >95% of variance when including TPMT*16 along with the most common variants TPMT*2, *3A, and *3C, compared to 70% without TPMT*16 (32973300). Five out of ten variant effect predictors tested by CPIC staff predict that the TPMT*16-defining SNV, c.488G>A (p.R163H), impairs protein function.

*2.findings_raw: TPMT*2 is assigned no function based on definitive evidence. TPMT.2 decreased protein expression has been attributed to rapid degradation by the proteasome (9177237, 16220112). Ten out of ten variant effect predictors tested by CPIC staff predict that the TPMT*2-defining SNV, c.238G>C (p.A80P), impairs protein function.

*3A.findings_raw: TPMT*3A is assigned no function based on definitive evidence. Erythrocytes from individuals heterozygous for TPMT*3A exhibited intermediate enzymatic activity, while erythrocytes from individuals homozygous for TPMT*3A or heterozygous for TPMT*3A in combination with another no function allele exhibited low enzymatic activity (9103127, 9246020, 9931346, 15226673, 23252716, 31005613). Patients carrying TPMT*3A alleles exhibited increased plasma concentrations of TGNs, decreased plasma concentrations of methylated metabolites, and tolerate lower doses of thiopurines (10580024, 11304783, 19057372, 23585236, 29387964, 33205673, 33928426). In vitro studies found that TPMT.3A protein expression and enzymatic activity is substantially decreased or undetectable relative to TPMT.1 in yeast cells (8644731, 9177237), mammalian cells (16220112,18708949, 8561894), and patient erythrocytes (9177237, 8644731, 8561894). Loss of TPMT.3A protein expression is attributed to rapid degradation by the proteasome (16220112, 9177237, 15967990). Seven and eight out of ten variant effect predictors tested by CPIC staff predict that the TPMT*3A-defining SNVs, c.460G>A (p.A154T) and c.719A>G (p.Y240C), impair protein function, respectively.

*3B.findings_raw: TPMT*3B is assigned no function based on definitive evidence. Patients carrying TPMT*3B alleles exhibited increased plasma concentrations of TGNs, increased DNA-incorporated thioguanine, decreased plasma concentrations of methylated metabolites, and tolerated lower doses of thiopurines (23585236, 29387964, 33928426, 33205673). TPMT.3B decreased protein expression is attributed to rapid degradation by the proteasome (16220112, 9177237) as well as TPMT.3B aggresome formation (15967990). Seven out of ten variant effect predictors tested by CPIC staff predict that the TPMT*3B-defining SNV, c.460G>A (p.A154T), impairs protein function.

*4.findings_raw: TPMT*4 is assigned no function based on strong evidence. *45.findings_raw: TPMT*45 is assigned no function based on limited evidence. A patient genotyped TPMT*1/*45 exhibited low TPMT enzymatic activity and a plasma 6-TGN concentration above the therapeutic range (33273844). TPMT*46 is assigned no function based on the *33 SNV (c.487C>T; p.R163C).

*6.findings_raw: TPMT*6 is assigned no function based on moderate evidence. Erythrocytes from an individual genotyped TPMT*1/*6 exhibited intermediate enzymatic activity toward 6-MP (9246020). An individual carrying TPMT*6 experienced severe leukopenia following standard azathioprine dosing (39696474). In vitro studies using mammalian cell expression systems demonstrate that TPMT.6 protein expression is substantially decreased compared to TPMT.1 (16220112). Additionally, TPMT.6 exhibited reduced substrate affinity for 6-TG, reduced clearance of 6-TG and 6-MP, and enzymatic activity was decreased by 60-80% in vitro (16220112, 18708949). Clinically, erythrocytes from individuals genotyped TPMT*1/*8 exhibited intermediate enzymatic activity (9931346, 27564568, 39182670). Ten out of ten variant effect predictors tested by CPIC staff predict that the TPMT*8-defining SNV, c.644G>A (p.R215H), does not impair protein function. Clinically, erythrocytes from individuals genotyped TPMT*1/*9 exhibited intermediate activity (15226673, 18602085, 23252716, 30840585, 31005613). Five out of ten variant effect predictors tested by CPIC staff predict that the TPMT*9-defining SNV, c.356A>C (p.K119T), impairs protein function.
